text:
NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>Across the source collage, the upper-left high-angle view shows the tall glazed A-frame, a projecting lower sloped-glass annex, and an elevated terrace; the upper-right and lower-left views confirm the front hierarchy, exterior stair, and open dining bay beneath the terrace. The lower-right view shows the attached timber-clad wall, while the interior panel confirms the tall glazed gable and exposed roof framing. The current model has these main elements, including a separate upper canopy with supports and a lower terrace fascia, but the front annex is narrower than in the source, the side cladding reads as flat peach panels, and the upper canopy looks broader and heavier. The open column bay is present in the current entry view and remains distinct from the terrace slab.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: The lower sloped-glass annex is visibly narrower than the source front panel, reducing the prominent glazed frontage beside the entry.
action: Widen and deepen this attached annex to match the source frontage while retaining the entry and open column bay.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="right">problem: The source side wall reads as warm timber cladding with distinct panel joints and relief; the current wall is a mostly flat peach surface with only thin seam lines.
action: Add the source-like timber finish and clearer panel joints or shallow reveals across the existing wall.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="oblique">problem: The separate upper canopy appears broader and heavier than the modest projecting canopy in the source, competing with the A-frame roof and terrace.
action: Reduce the upper canopy footprint and visual thickness, retaining its supports and keeping it distinct from the lower terrace slab/fascia.</issue>
<keep>
Glazed A-frame main roof silhouette and exposed framing.
Exterior stair rising to the upper terrace.
Lower terrace fascia and the open dining bay beneath it.
</keep>
